a10_worth_attempting_qualifier: Worth exactly ONE bounded seed42 screen of the corrected design, with a hard stop if it fails. Four consecutive improvement experiments (A9.6/A9.7/A9.8/A9.9) have failed, so prior probability of clearing the gate is modest; this is the last specialist attempt.

recommended_strategy.name: frozen_a9_embedding_regularized_head
recommended_strategy.description: Freeze the entire A9 encoder+gate and use its 128-d embedding as FIXED features for attack rows. Train ONLY a small, strongly-regularized attack-family head (linear or a single shallow GELU layer) with high dropout, weight decay, label smoothing, and tempered (less aggressive) class weights. Keep A9 Head 1 as the frozen binary router. Use a generalization-aware validation criterion / earlier stopping. This directly fixes A9.9's two failure modes: it preserves the shared representation A9.9 discarded, and a tiny regularized head shrinks the validation-to-test gap.
changes_from_a99: Reuse the FROZEN A9 encoder embedding instead of training a new encoder from scratch (restores shared representation).
Much smaller head: linear or one shallow layer, vs A9.9's [256,128] independent encoder (reduces overfit).
Stronger regularization: higher dropout + weight decay + label smoothing.
Tempered / less aggressive attack-family class weights to protect rare-class precision (avoid the Shellcode over-prediction and the A9.6/A9.9 RC5 pattern).
Earlier stopping / generalization-aware validation selection to close the val->test gap.

expected_benefit: Addresses both A9.9 failure modes. Realistic oracle attack-family macro-F1 ~0.50-0.53 (3-seed mean if it advances); a fair chance to recover rare-class macro toward A9 0.385669 by protecting Shellcode/Worms precision. Binary unchanged (router frozen).
expected_risk: Modest upside, real chance of another below-gate result. A9.7/A9.8 already showed that adding Head-2 capacity on the shared embedding gives only +0.0045 attack-family (within the ~0.0143 seed-noise band), and intrinsic RC1 overlap caps the ceiling near ~0.60. If the seed42 screen does not clear 0.515429 with rare >= 0.385669, the specialist direction is exhausted.
why_this_avoids_a99_failure_mode: A9.9 failed because the independent encoder overfit (val 0.5863 -> test 0.4747) and lost the benign-informed shared representation, regressing Fuzzers/Shellcode/Worms. A9.10 freezes and reuses that representation and trains only a tiny regularized head, so there is far less to overfit and the generalizing features are retained; tempered weights protect rare precision.

rejection_option.reason: A fully defensible choice now: A9.6 (loss weight), A9.7/A9.8 (branch capacity), and A9.9 (independent specialist) have all failed to beat A9. The attack-family ceiling (~0.50-0.60) is dominated by intrinsic Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits overlap (RC1). If main control prefers, freeze A9 as the final UNSW model with documented limitations and move to federated/security/XAI scope rather than spend another run.
